proposal.name: Check Python attempts one size larger

plan.name: Check Python attempts one size larger
plan.summary: For each eligible exhaustive Python application invocation, agreement one size larger will require its authenticated recording to pass the same Init, Next, declared-outcome and every-step checks used at the ratified bounds, evaluated with the larger constants, as well as matching TLC's state count and depth; environment-only omissions use the next environment bounds from that larger size, preserving parameter exclusions and the existing prerequisite and sibling-result rules. Reuse the streaming, batched conformance path and shared TLC resource budget, with exploration, recording conversion and conformance sharing the existing six-minute per-invocation allowance after the three-minute larger model check: an unfinished or operationally unavailable conformance check claims nothing under D-0070, parent cancellation propagates, and completed disagreements or invalid execution evidence still fail, with private resources cleaned on every exit. Add optional Conformance evidence of type PythonApplicationConformance to each PythonApplicationLarger record, separate from base evidence, preserving counts even on disagreement and binding the larger inputs, constants, logical TLC results and counterexample in JSON and portable fingerprints; larger failures and Markdown receipts name the invocation and offending action and before/after states or invalid initial state, and old receipts without this evidence retain their count-only wording. Extend the existing counter-model fake and receipt tests without weakening their assertions, add pinned-TLC integration regressions for the equal-count 2-to-4 error and a correct counter, and exercise deadlines, batched protocol-scale recordings, cleanup and existing fixtures so checks either finish within their allowance or explicitly claim nothing. Update SPEC.md, citing [#881's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-881.json), the README's larger-check description and docs/python.md to distinguish Go explorers and count-only drivers from Python applications whose attempts are checked, and to describe the stronger verdict, evidence and shared time allowance.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationLargerRejectsEqualCountWrongStep881
tests.says: An application reaching 0, 1, 2 and 4 one size larger fails despite matching TLC's four states and four levels, identifies Inc from 2 to 4, and keeps its passing base evidence; a correct counter passes at the larger constants.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationLargerChecksInitialStates881
tests.says: An invalid larger initial state fails Init even when the larger exploration has the same state count and depth as TLC.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationLargerChecksEveryStep881
tests.says: Omitting an enabled step only at the larger size fails the larger attempt check while keeping successful transition and base evidence.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationLargerConformanceDeadline881
tests.says: A larger conformance check that cannot finish exhausts the bounded allowance, claims no larger agreement and does not fail otherwise successful base verification.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationLargerReceiptExplainsWrongStep881
tests.says: Explicit and legacy Markdown receipts explain the larger Inc step from 2 to 4 in What failed, and JSON round trips retain the larger conformance evidence and fingerprint without replacing base coverage.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and five acceptance tests covering larger Python conformance, timeouts, and receipt evidence. Check 1 passed: all five tests fail on the base checkout as required; the planned build requires a person to merge.
